name: A Nile Cruise
tagline: A genuinely classic way to see ancient Egypt, sailing between Luxor and Aswan past temples that have watched the same river for thousands of years.
highlight: Waking up on deck to find the boat has moored beside a temple overnight, stepping straight off the gangplank into Kom Ombo before the day's heat sets in.
shortDescription: A multi-night journey between Luxor and Aswan, the classic way to see the Nile's temples at Edfu and Kom Ombo without repeated hotel changes.
metaDescription: A Nile cruise travel guide: Edfu, Kom Ombo, life aboard, food and how to plan a multi-night cruise between Luxor and Aswan.
nearestAirport: Luxor International Airport (LXR), or Aswan International Airport (ASW)
knownFor: Temple stops at Edfu and Kom Ombo, riverside scenery
goodFor: A relaxed, comfortable way to see multiple temples

image.file: File:Movenpick Radamis II Cruise Ship on the Nile River (4058006543).jpg
image.alt: A Nile cruise ship sailing between Luxor and Aswan

intro: A Nile cruise is genuinely the classic way to see Upper Egypt, a multi-night journey between Luxor and Aswan that covers ancient temple sites at Edfu and Kom Ombo without the hassle of repeated hotel changes.

The river itself is genuinely part of the experience, its banks unchanged in essence for millennia — palm groves, mudbrick villages and farmland worked much as it always has been, right alongside the boat's route.

Most visitors genuinely book a three- or four-night cruise, sailing between Luxor and Aswan with guided stops at each temple along the way, all meals and cabin accommodation included in a single package.

whyVisit.intro: A Nile cruise's case rests on genuinely combining efficient sightseeing with a uniquely relaxed, scenic way to travel.

points.title: It's genuinely the most efficient way to see multiple temples
points.text: Edfu and Kom Ombo are both reached without a single extra hotel change.

points.title: The river scenery is genuinely part of the appeal
points.text: Palm groves and riverside village life passing by, largely unchanged for centuries.

points.title: Edfu's temple is genuinely one of Egypt's best preserved
points.text: Its roof and walls remarkably intact, giving a real sense of how these temples once looked complete.

points.title: Kom Ombo's dual design is genuinely unique
points.text: A rare temple built as mirrored twin sanctuaries dedicated to two different gods.

points.title: It's genuinely a comfortable, all-inclusive way to travel
points.text: Meals, cabin and guided excursions all bundled into a single, relaxed itinerary.

attractionsIntro: A Nile cruise's essential sights combine genuinely life aboard the boat with major temple stops along the route.

attractions.name: The Nile cruise ship

image.file: File:Movenpick Radamis II Cruise Ship on the Nile River (4058006543).jpg
image.alt: A Nile cruise ship on the river

attractions.text: Genuinely a floating hotel for the journey, most boats offering cabins, a sun deck, dining rooms and often a small pool.
attractions.tip: Genuinely book a cabin with a river-facing balcony if your budget allows — the views are worth it.

attractions.name: The Temple of Horus at Edfu

image.alt: The Temple of Horus at Edfu

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Egypt's best-preserved ancient temples, its roof and walls remarkably intact after being buried in sand for centuries.
attractions.tip: Genuinely reached by horse-drawn carriage from the dock, part of the classic Edfu stop experience.

attractions.name: The Temple of Kom Ombo
attractions.text: Genuinely unique among Egyptian temples, built as mirrored twin sanctuaries dedicated to two different gods, Sobek and Horus.
attractions.tip: Genuinely visit at sunset if your cruise schedule allows — the temple is especially striking in golden light.

attractions.name: Kom Ombo's twin sanctuaries

image.alt: The columned courtyard of Kom Ombo Temple

attractions.text: Genuinely a rare architectural symmetry, with matching entrances, halls and sanctuaries mirrored down the temple's central axis.
attractions.tip: Genuinely spot the ancient crocodile mummies displayed in the temple's small on-site museum.

attractions.name: Edfu's hypostyle hall

image.alt: The hypostyle hall at the Temple of Edfu

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the most complete surviving examples of ancient Egyptian temple architecture, its full roof structure still intact.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a real, rare chance to imagine these temples as they originally looked, roof and all.

attractions.name: Nile riverbank scenery

image.alt: The Nile riverbank between Luxor and Aswan

attractions.text: Genuinely part of the cruise's real appeal, palm groves, farmland and village life passing slowly by the boat's rails.
attractions.tip: Genuinely the sun deck offers the best vantage point for watching the riverbank scenery unfold.

attractions.name: A felucca crossing the cruise route

image.alt: A traditional felucca sailing near the cruise route

attractions.text: Genuinely a common sight along the way, traditional wooden sailboats still working the same stretch of river.
attractions.tip: Genuinely many cruises include a short felucca excursion of their own, separate from the main boat.

thingsToDoIntro: A Nile cruise genuinely rewards embracing its slower pace, alternating temple visits with real time on the water.

thingsToDo.title: Sail between temples on the cruise boat

image.file: File:Abercrombie & Kent river cruise ship R01.jpg
image.alt: Sailing on a Nile cruise boat

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed core of the experience, watching the riverbank pass by between each guided temple stop.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely much of the sailing happens overnight, so daytime hours are largely free for sightseeing or relaxing.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the Temple of Horus at Edfu

image.file: File:Temple of Edfu, Statue of Horus, Egypt.jpg
image.alt: Exploring the Temple of Horus at Edfu

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential stop, walking through one of Egypt's most completely preserved ancient temples.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely the horse-drawn carriage ride from the dock is a memorable part of the Edfu stop.

thingsToDo.title: Visit the twin temple of Kom Ombo

image.file: File:By ovedc - Temple of Kom Ombo - 43.jpg
image.alt: Visiting the twin temple of Kom Ombo

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely fascinating architectural puzzle, tracing the temple's mirrored design dedicated to two different gods.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely don't miss the small crocodile mummy museum on the temple grounds.

thingsToDo.title: Watch the riverbank scenery pass by

image.alt: Watching the Nile riverbank from a cruise boat

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely underrated part of the cruise, simply watching daily riverside life unfold from the sun deck.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely bring a good book or simply enjoy the unhurried pace between temple stops.

thingsToDo.title: Enjoy a traditional show onboard

image.file: File:'Raqs Sharqi' performance on cruise boat 'Topaz' on Nile River..JPG
image.alt: A traditional dance performance aboard a Nile cruise boat

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely fun evening addition on many cruises, traditional music and dance performances after dinner.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely check your cruise's evening schedule — these shows are usually included, not an extra cost.

thingsToDo.title: Relax on the sun deck
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential part of the cruise experience, whether by the small pool or simply taking in the view.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely the sun deck offers the best photo opportunities as the boat passes each new stretch of riverbank.

bestTime.headline: October to April for the mildest temperatures on deck and ashore
bestTime.summary: A Nile cruise genuinely runs year-round, though winter and shoulder season offer far more comfortable conditions for the temple stops.

seasons.text: Genuinely the mildest temperatures for both onboard time and temple excursions, also the busiest season.
Genuinely warm but manageable heat with thinner crowds than peak winter.
Genuinely intense heat ashore, though the boat's air-conditioned cabins and pool offer real relief.

bestTime.avoid: Booking a cruise without checking your cabin's air conditioning — genuinely essential given Upper Egypt's heat most of the year.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Nile cruise noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely a reputable operator with recent reviews — quality varies significantly between cruise companies.
Choose genuinely a river-view or balcony cabin if your budget allows — it's worth the upgrade.
Pack genuinely modest clothing for temple visits, alongside swimwear for the sun deck.
Bring genuinely small cash for tipping guides and crew, expected throughout the cruise.
Confirm genuinely which excursions are included versus optional extras before booking.
Check genuinely your cabin's air conditioning, especially important outside the winter months.

faq.q: How many nights should a Nile cruise be?
faq.a: Three to four nights genuinely covers the classic Luxor to Aswan route comfortably, with stops at Edfu and Kom Ombo.

faq.q: What's included in a Nile cruise price?
faq.a: Genuinely most packages include your cabin, all meals, and guided shore excursions at each temple stop — check specifics before booking.

faq.q: Do you need to book a Nile cruise in advance?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely recommended, especially for the best cabins in peak winter season, when demand is highest.

faq.q: What is a Nile cruise known for?
faq.a: Genuinely being the classic, efficient way to see Upper Egypt's temples at Edfu and Kom Ombo, combined with the Nile's own timeless riverside scenery.

faq.q: Can you do a Nile cruise in the other direction, from Aswan to Luxor?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — cruises run both directions, so the route works equally well starting from either city.

faq.q: Is a Nile cruise suitable for families?
faq.a: Generally yes, genuinely — most boats offer a relaxed pace and a pool, though check specific excursion intensity for younger children.
